From someone who doesn't really understand networking on this level: what is the difference between having the proxy resolve the DNS compared to having the client resolve it? At the face of it I personally think it sounds better to resolve it client side as you're not going out to any other server, what are the differences here?
Could you elaborate on DNS leaks? I fixed the Webrtc leak in Firefox but I've never fixed anything related to DNS. Everything checked out on ipleak.net when I was connected to my VPN, though.

So VPN typically solves the DNS leak. The issue is common on tor. Tor uses socks5 as a protocol between your browser and the tor program. The problem is that socks is a tcp protocol while dns is a udp protocol. You can't do udp over socks. That means that the dns is routed the exact same as it always was when you use tor out of the box.

To fix this you set the remote_socks_dns which basically says that you can send a tcp message to the socks and whatever is at the other end of it will be able to figure out what you want, which tor exit nodes do.

VPN on the other hand makes the vpn integral to the network connection meaning no data can leave your computer without being routed to the exit ip, no matter the protocol. The issue that worries me and I'd like to know more about it is when you make your local network connection dhcp helps configure aspects of the network based on the environment so you don't have to ender in a lot of settings. One aspect is the dns server. The VPN in say Tokyo may be contacting the verizon dns server for your region. Is that what's going on, is that a security flaw? I actually wish I knew these things. I'm pretty confident in the case of tor that the tor exit node is using what it considers to be dns.
